ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The schematic diagram is a bar comparison of the proportions of three freight transport modes in the national total for four regions. The legend shows that the black bars are railway transport, the diagonal-line bars are water transport, and the blank bars are road transport. The railway transport bar of the Bohai Rim region is relatively high, at about around 20%; the railway transport bar of the "Yangtze River Delta" region is obviously lower than that of the Bohai Rim region, while its water transport bar is the highest, obviously higher than the other transport modes. Reasoning: The question stem points out that the "Yangtze River Delta" and the Bohai Rim are both located in China's eastern plains, so the difference in railway construction between the two places should not mainly be attributed to terrain undulation. In the diagram, the proportion of water transport in the "Yangtze River Delta" is prominent, indicating that this region has developed river-and-lake waterways and a dense river network. A dense river network will cut across railway lines; railway laying requires a large number of river-crossing bridges, increasing construction difficulty and cost. Therefore, the most important restricting factor is the dense river network.
